spec_match.rationale: The closedby matrix is measured on real dialogs in all three states rather than described, which is how the modality-dependent missing-value default (none for show(), closerequest for showModal()) is shown rather than asserted. The dismissal mechanism is presented as an event-ordering question, which is what the HTML change actually is.

interactive.rationale: A live matrix that opens and closes real modal dialogs while you wait, plus three openable dialogs to try Escape and backdrop clicks against; an event recorder that marks the moment of closure inside the sequence; and a menu-over-a-list checklist that detects each gesture and judges it from the menu's state rather than from self-report.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames the change as choosing which event means 'click' — pointerdown versus click — and names the two bugs that follow from the earlier choice, which is the pull request's own framing.

edge_cases.rationale: Invalid and empty closedby values, case-insensitive keyword matching, the popover attribute's opposite invalid-value default, a dialog whose only exit is its own button, and a menu item activation that closes the popover for a reason that is neither light dismiss nor a close request.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/6209615938322432 on the index and all three concept pages, with WHATWG HTML PR 11536, the closedby attribute section and MDN's Popover API.

conformance.rationale: Eight immutable assertions: popover and closedby exist; keyword matching is case-insensitive; the missing-value default differs by modality; an invalid closedby never resolves to 'any'; dispatched input does not light-dismiss; the popover attribute's invalid-value default is manual; and CloseWatcher backs the close request.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Two browsers now. Chrome 150 (deno task drive): 3/3 pages, 27 assertions, the closedby matrix in all three states, case-insensitivity, invalid-value behaviour, the recorder's labelling, and synthetic input ignored. Chromium 141 (pre-change, weekly hardening 2026-09-13) driven with TRUSTED CDP input — Input.dispatchMouseEvent and Input.synthesizeScrollGesture: a real right-click outside closed the menu and the checklist rendered its old-behaviour fail verdict; a real left click outside closed it (pass); the recorder captured the close landing on the press (pointerdown → mousedown → POPOVER CLOSED, trusted=yes) and its non-click fallback wording handled mousedown correctly. The touch-drag row cannot self-record on a pre-change browser — the press closes the menu before any scroll event arrives, which is the bug itself; noted below. The conformance panel's untrusted probe events appeared in the recording correctly marked trusted=no.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the measured defaults, the event preceding the close, whether synthetic input was ignored, and a per-gesture pass or fail.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, buttons set background and colour together including the transparent menu items, 44px minimums on the page controls with a deliberate 36px inside the compact menu and toolbar, and the wide tables in their own scroll containers. The dialog backdrop is the one place a raw colour appears, as an alpha black that has no token.

accessibility.rationale: Every dialog is labelled by its heading; the popover menu carries an aria-label; results are announced through aria-live; the checklist verdicts are sentences rather than colour alone; and each gesture card names what should happen before you try it, so the expectation is readable without doing it.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The toolbar and button rows wrap; the list scroller uses overscroll-behavior:contain so a drag inside it does not chain to the page; the recorder table scrolls in its own container; the dialogs are max-width constrained. Mobile is the class where the scroll gesture matters most, and the demo is built for a touch drag rather than a mouse wheel.

openQuestions.title: Complete the scroll row of the checklist with trusted touch input on a corrected browser
openQuestions.detail: Trusted CDP input (dispatchMouseEvent, synthesizeScrollGesture) has now completed the right-click and click rows, and on pre-change Chromium 141 it demonstrated why the scroll row cannot record there: the press dismisses the menu before the first scroll event, so judge('scroll') never runs — the exact bug the feature fixes. On a Chrome ≥145 the same synthesizeScrollGesture at a list point clear of the popover should complete the third row and move the checklist to 3/3 automatically. The harness exists (weekly hardening drive script); it only needs a corrected browser.

openQuestions.title: Compare against a browser with the old behaviour
openQuestions.detail: RESOLVED in effect on 2026-09-13: Chromium 141 predates the change and the one-sided branch has now run. The recorder showed the close landing on the press (sequence pointerdown → mousedown, trusted), and the survives-the-gesture checklist rendered its old-behaviour fail copy for the right-click case exactly as written. Kept as a note: the recorder's old-behaviour explainer names pointerdown as the preceding event, while 141 lands it one event later on mousedown — the generic fallback sentence covered it, so no page change is needed.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible popover and dialog light dismiss
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use closedby on a dialog to opt into light dismiss explicitly rather than reimplementing outside-click handling, and let the platform own focus and dismissal.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The three demonstration dialogs use closedby="any", "closerequest" and "none" with no dismissal code of any kind; the menu is a plain auto popover opened with popovertarget. Nothing on these pages implements outside-click handling, which is what makes the recordings measurements of the browser rather than of the page.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: The matrix reads closedBy back from real dialogs; the recorder's close entries come from beforetoggle, not from a handler that closed anything.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle a popover from a button without javascript
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Open overlays with popovertarget rather than script so the platform manages the top layer, focus and dismissal.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both popovers are opened by popovertarget buttons. The only scripted show/hide is in the synthetic-input control, and it now marks its own close so the recorder does not attribute it to the preceding event — a bug this build shipped briefly and caught in its own drive output.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: The recorder now prints '▸ POPOVER CLOSED (by this page)' and refuses to interpret the sequence around it.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce the result of a gesture the user performs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce outcomes in text, and do not require the user to interpret a colour or to self-report what happened.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each gesture card's verdict is a sentence written from a measurement taken 160ms after the gesture; the summary counts progress in a live region. The user performs the gesture; the page decides what it means.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive scrolls the list programmatically and asserts the scroll card's verdict text changed from its untried state.

summary: Three concepts about an event-ordering change. Everything reachable without trusted input is measured — the closedby matrix including the modality-dependent default, the invalid-value behaviour, and the fact that dispatched input is correctly ignored — and the three gestures that need a real pointer are handed to the reader with the page doing the judging. The build's own scripted cleanup briefly made the recorder claim a click had dismissed a popover it had closed itself; the recorder now labels a scripted close and declines to interpret it.
